Ambush
ăm´bŏŏsh
n., v. (a concealed force; rendering Hebrew arab)
From Old French embuscher, to hide in the woods. An ambush is a force that exists before it is seen.

Biblical Definition

An ambush is a hidden force set to strike. Joshua's taking of Ai turns on one: “And Joshua rose up… and chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour, and sent them away by night… lie in wait against the city, even behind the city” (Jos 8:3–4). Jehoshaphat's victory reverses the picture — the LORD set ambushments against the enemy while Judah merely sang (2Ch 20:22). Jeremiah warns Israel that God Himself may become the hidden adversary, and Proverbs warns the young man that sinners lay wait for their own blood (Pro 1:18).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines ambush as a private or concealed station where troops lie in wait to attack by surprise; and the troops so posted.

expand to see more

AMBUSH, n. A private or concealed station, where troops lie in wait to attack their enemy by surprise.

2. The troops posted in a concealed place, for attacking by surprise.

3. A lying in wait, for the purpose of attacking by surprise.

Key Scripture

Jos 8:4 — "And he commanded them, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in wait against the city, even behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready:"

2Ch 20:22 — "And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten. And"

Pro 1:18 — "And they lay wait for their own blood; they lurk privily for their own lives."

Jdg 9:34 — "And Abimelech rose up, and all the people that were with him, by night, and they laid wait against Shechem in four companies."

Modern Corruption

Spiritual danger is imagined as a frontal assault, so believers watch the road ahead and are taken from the side — which is the only way an ambush ever works.

expand to see more

2 Chronicles 20:22 is the passage worth memorizing, because the ambush belongs to God: when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir. Judah's contribution was worship; the concealed force was the LORD's. Believers facing odds they cannot compute are not told to devise cleverness but to praise, on the understanding that the field contains forces they cannot see.

Proverbs 1 applies the figure to sin's self-defeat: they lay wait for their own blood; they lurk privily for their own lives. The ambush the wicked set is, in the long providence of God, the trap they fall into. That does not make vigilance unnecessary, but it does mean the believer is never facing an enemy whose schemes are outside God's government.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew arab (H693), to lie in wait; the noun maarab (H3993), an ambush — the vocabulary of Joshua 8 and Judges 9.

expand to see more

Hebrew arab (H693) — to lie in wait, ambush; Joshua 8:4, Judges 9:34, Proverbs 1:11.

Hebrew maarab (H3993) — ambush, lying in wait; Joshua 8:9, 2 Chronicles 13:13.

Greek enedra (G1747) — ambush, plot; Acts 23:16 and 25:3, the plot against Paul.

Usage

"“Lie in wait against the city, even behind the city” — the taking of Ai."

"“The LORD set ambushments” — while Judah sang."

"“They lay wait for their own blood” — the trap that catches its maker."
